We need to list events on both calendars to check conflicts. Then create event if no conflicts.

First, list events on cal-alice around that date. Use list_events with timeMin and timeMax covering the day. The event start: 2026-11-02 09:30 America/New_York => UTC? New York in November is EDT? Actually November 2 2026, DST ends Nov 1 2026? In US, DST ends first Sunday in November, which in 2026 is Nov 1. So Nov 2 is standard time EST (UTC-5). So 09:30 EST = 14:30 UTC. Good matches 14:30 Europe/London. London in November after last Sunday of October (Oct 25 2026?) Actually UK DST ends last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is Oct 25. So Nov 2 is GMT (UTC+0). So 14:30 London = 14:30 UTC. So both align. So event start UTC 2026-11-02T14:30:00Z, end 30 min later 14:59? Actually 30-min event ends at 15:00 UTC. So end 2026-11-02T15:00:00Z.

We need to list events on cal-alice and cal-bob for that date range, perhaps from 2026-11-02T14:00Z to 2026-11-02T16:00Z.

We'll call list_events for both calendars. Then examine for any overlapping events.

Let's start with list_events on cal-alice.
